One of these two tasks will be performed next. Option 1: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences.
Option 2: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
--- END OF PROVIDED PORTION ---

Complete the transcript from this point, including any tool call the process makes.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself. Think of it like looking up a word in a dictionary, but to understand the definition, you have to look up another word, which leads to another, until you reach a simple word you already know. In code, the function breaks the main problem down into smaller, similar sub-problems until it hits a "base case" that is simple enough to solve directly. Once the base case is solved, the answers bubble back up through all the previous function calls to give you the final solution.
